# Components

Which components the system carries: its inventory, picked from the catalogue.

## The five answers

| Question | Answer | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which component families does it need? | Core, plus content and media | Readers need sections, navigation and little else. |
| How far does the inventory reach? | Only what today's screens use | Actions are rare, so the components today's pages use cover them. |
| How does a component earn its place? | A use scenario needs it | A component joins only when reading needs it. |
| When does a component get another look? | Only when the meaning changes | Pages stay calm when a component changes only with its meaning. |
| Where do components do the most work? | Articles | Components sit inside and around articles. |

## Where it lands

- Button
- Input
- Control
- Badge
- Card
- Table
- Tabs
- Overlay

## When to use what

| Situation | Use | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No component in the inventory fits | plain text, a link or a heading | a new component for one article | Readers come for the words; extra parts pull the eye away from them. |
